text:
mohit_support: heads up — acme-inc reports intermittent 401s right after our api key rotation in eu-prod. rotated key at 03:40 UTC via Vault, rollout finished, but ~5% of their lambda invocations return 401. only observed from their eu lambda pool.

mohit_support: repro log snippet from their request id 01F8Z2JX: 
```
> curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"unauthorized","code":401,"message":"Invalid API key"}
```

alicia_sre: pinging infra — did the rollout finish fully or did some pods miss the env update? :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy-ci/3.14.7 -> eu-prod finished at 03:42 UTC, rollout status: 100% (12/12). no failed pods reported.

ben_support: do we have their request ids + x-request-id? i want to correlate on edge logs. also which client runtime? they said nodejs lambda.

mohit_support: they sent a small sample set (10k requests). failing requests have X-Edge-Cache: HIT and Authorization header contains older key material (looks like the pre-rotation key). successful ones use new key. so seems like some hosts are still using old creds.

carla_security: could be KMS unwrap mismatch if key alias rotated, but that would fail for all clients. the fact it's partial suggests caching or sidecar not reloading. check Vault Agent template refresh and lease expiry.

alicia_sre: running quick check on one affected pod from eu-node-7: kubectl exec -it pod/eu-lambda-processor-7 -- cat /var/run/secrets/redwood/apikey -> shows OLD_KEY_ABC123. interestingly the pod restarted after rollout but the sidecar (vault-agent) process PID unchanged.

ben_support: ah that hints at the env being baked into the lambda container at start and the agent template failing to rewrite file while process kept original env. can lambdas hot-swap env? their runtime sets env at init and caches header.

mohit_support: repro steps I ran (dev cluster):
1) create Vault secret version v1 -> app reads key OK
2) rotate secret in Vault to v2
3) agent template configured with `vault agent -config=/etc/vault/agent/config.hcl` (template `{\"apikey\": \"{{ with secret \"secret/data/redwood/apikey\" }}{{ .Data.data.value }}{{ end }}\" }`)
4) template file updated on disk, but process that reads env file did not reload until container restart -> some instances keep using old key.

alicia_sre: do we see any Vault agent logs on that node?

alicia_sre: `kubectl logs vault-agent-eu-node-7` shows repeated `template: render succeeded` at 03:40:05 but then at 03:40:35 a `lease expired` event and a re-auth attempt. agent recovered, but our agent config had template_refresh_interval: 10s and a short token_renew_window set to 30s. jitter + short lease => race where file was updated but the env-consuming process had a short caching window and didn't pick up new content.

carla_security: also saw that the hash of the file on disk changed but the lambda execution environment keeps a cached header value in memory for performance. for long-running lambda containers (warm starts) they only read env on cold start. if rotation happens mid-warm period the function will continue with old value until the runtime restarts.

ben_support: that matches symptoms — requests coming from warm caches (edge + warm lambda) showing old Authorization header and getting 401 after server-side rotation. edge cache HIT indicates client is still sending old header; edge didn't reject until backend validated.

mohit_support: workaround we applied for acme-inc: forced sidecar restart + orchestrated rolling restart of their lambda pool (via our control plane bounce) plus purge of CDN edge cache for their tenant. after that failures dropped to 0. customer confirmed.

alicia_sre: steps we executed (worked):
```
# force restart vault-agent sidecar on eu nodes for that deployment
kubectl rollout restart deployment/acme-lambda-processor -n eu-prod --field-selector metadata.name=acme-lambda-processor
# then purge edge cache for tenant
curl -X PURGE https://edge.eu.redwood.ai/tenant/acme-inc --header \"X-Auth-Token: ${EDGE_OPERATOR_TOKEN}\"
```

carla_security: short-term mitigation notes posted to internal runbook. long-term fixes recommended:
- increase Vault agent template_refresh and add jitter to avoid simultaneous lease renew races
- extend token renew window to avoid leaving brief periods where template writes happen during re-auth
- add post-rotation lifecycle hook that signals application pods to reload credentials (SIGHUP or in-process endpoint)
- add a staged client rollout: rotate consumer keys in batches and pause warm runtimes before rotation
- add edge-level validation that rejects requests with legacy keys earlier (and return 403 with special code) so issues fail fast and are visible to clients

ben_support: filing escalation ticket to track follow-ups and change requests. assigning to eng-runtime and security for config changes.

mohit_support: customer ops confirmed full recovery after rolling restart + cache purge. they asked for a postmortem and a change to rotation docs to call out warm runtime behavior.

alicia_sre: will add postmortem + runbook updates. summary for postmortem: root cause = agent-template + short lease/renew-window race + warm lambda env caching -> partial use of old key. impact = intermittent 401s for ~5% of requests for acme-inc eu pool, duration ~12m until workaround.

carla_security: action items:
- eng-runtime: implement optional cred hot-reload endpoint and document SIGHUP behavior (owner: @alicia_sre)
- infra: tune vault-agent defaults for template refresh and renew window (owner: @devops)
- support: update rotation playbook + customer communication template (owner: @ben_support)

ben_support: noted. closing thread once postmortem doc link posted. :thumbsup:

mohit_support: thanks everyone — acme-inc on call appreciated the quick turnaround. closing on my side once changes are live. :white_check_mark:
